title: A quasi-compact surjective flat morphism is submersive on the underlying topological spaces
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a quasi-compact, surjective and flat morphism detects open and closed subsets on the source: a subset of the target is open, respectively closed, exactly when its preimage is, so the morphism is submersive (statement lines 5060-5070). The counted proof reduces first by locality on the target and by replacing the quasi-compact source with the disjoint union of finitely many affine opens, then handles the affine case by writing a subset with closed preimage as the image of a closed subscheme, using that generalizations lift along the flat map to get that its complement is stable under generalization, and applying the affine criterion that specialization-stable subsets are closed (proof lines 3072-3095). It is H2: the argument is a complete reduction chain carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard topological and algebraic criteria.
